newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat condition improves with rains.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat condition improves with rains.

text.p: Wet weather over the last two weeks improved the condition of Texas's wheat crop, although excessive moisture has caused some problems, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.

"The additional moisture was beneficial in most areas. However, there were some isolated fields with standing water that could cause problems," the report said. "Irrigated fields in the High Plains continued to make progress. Dryland fields have improved some with light snowfall over the past weeks."
Texas wheat was rated 75 percent of normal, up from 70 percent two weeks ago and 38 percent last year.

Wheat was rated nine percent excellent, 45 good, 38 fair, seven poor and one very poor. The comparative numbers for two weeks earlier were nine percent excellent, 40 percent good, 34 percent fair, 15 percent poor and two percent very poor.
Livestock conditions remained good, with improved markets reported in many areas, the report said.
Range and pasture conditions were rated five percent excellent, 29 percent good, 41 percent fair, 18 percent poor and seven percent very poor.
